title: Director of Design
description:
About Mendocino Farms
  
At Mendocino Farms, we do a lot more than just sell sandwiches and salads. We are a fast-casual restaurant brand on a mission to bring people together through fresh, culinary-driven food and unmatched hospitality. As we continue our aggressive growth trajectory across new and existing markets, we are seeking a dynamic, analytical, and hands-on leader to elevate our total rewards structure.
  
Our Core Values and Mantras
  

* Sell Happy: The foundational philosophy that goes beyond serving meals to actively uplifting and improving every guest's day.
* Food Should Make People Feel Good: A commitment to using high-quality, whole, and thoughtfully sourced ingredients that make eating well easy.
* Be Culinary Explorers: A passion for combining fresh ingredients and bold flavors in unexpected, gourmet ways.
* Turn the Ordinary into the Extraordinary: Treating every customer and team interaction as a chance to lift someone's spirits.
* Get Better Every Day (GBED): An internal mantra encouraging continuous learning, personal growth, and skill development.

Director of Design
  
  
**Reports To:** VP, Design & Construction
  
**FLSA Status:** Exempt
  
**Cost Center:** 9511
  
**Location:** Dallas, TX or Remote, USA
  
**Salary Range:** $117,000–$190,000 (Compensation is based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.)
  
  
Position Summary
  
Mendocino Farms is seeking a Director of Design to lead the evolution and delivery of our restaurant experience across new restaurants, remodels, refreshes, and strategic initiatives.
  
**This leader will own Mendo’s design function:** the restaurant prototype, design standards, internal and external design resources, and the systems that turn brand strategy into distinctive, functional, and scalable restaurants. You will partner closely with Operations, Culinary, Facilities, Construction, Real Estate, and Marketing to create environments that strengthen the guest experience while supporting efficient operations, disciplined investment, and growth.
  
This is an opportunity for a creative and operationally minded leader who can set a compelling design point of view, build a high-performing team and consultant network, and make practical decisions that balance quality, durability, speed, cost, and long-term unit performance as Mendocino Farms expands its restaurant footprint.
  
Core Responsibilities
  
Lead the Design Function
  

* Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop internal designers and external design resources; set clear expectations, effective working rhythms, and a high bar for quality and accountability.
* Resource Alignment: Align internal and external design resources to the development pipeline, identifying when specialized expertise is needed.
* Senior Design Leadership: Serve as the senior design leader for complex, high-visibility, or high-risk projects and decisions.

Own the Brand Environment and Design Standards
  

* Prototype & Standards Ownership: Own and evolve Mendo’s restaurant prototype, design standards, material palettes, finishes, furniture, fixtures, lighting, equipment integration, and reusable design details.
* Brand Consistency: Ensure every restaurant delivers a recognizable Mendo experience while adapting appropriately to site conditions, market needs, and business priorities.
* Brand Evolution: Use operating feedback, field learning, and market insight to keep the brand environment relevant, differentiated, and scalable.
* Creative Point of View: Set and elevate Mendo’s creative design point of view, translating brand strategy into memorable, functional restaurant environments that feel distinctive across markets and formats.

Improve Restaurant Operations Through Design
  

* Operational Design Standards: Maintain and evolve design standards that prioritize guest flow, ordering and pickup, digital and delivery activity, seating, accessibility, storage, serviceability, and day-to-day operations.
* Kitchen & BOH Planning: Partner with Operations, Culinary, Facilities, Construction, and equipment vendors to improve kitchen planning, back-of-house flow, equipment integration, team ergonomics, throughput, food safety, and maintainability.
* Post-Opening Learning: Incorporate post-opening learning into future layouts, prototypes, and specifications.

Drive Quality, Clarity, and Design Delivery
  

* Design Delivery: Oversee design delivery for new restaurants, remodels, and refresh programs from feasibility test fits and concepts through permit-ready documentation and design-related construction support.
* QA/QC & Phase Gates: Establish practical design QA/QC and phase-gate practices that produce complete, coordinated, code-aware, and timely deliverables.
* Cross-Functional Reviews: Lead cross-functional reviews using clear agendas, advance pre-reads, recommendations, concise decision requests, and thoroughly documented follow-through.
* Stakeholder Direction: Translate stakeholder input into clear direction for internal teams and consultants, surfacing risks and tradeoffs early.
* Constructability: Partner with Construction to protect design intent, improve constructability, and reduce design-related rework, RFIs, and change orders.

Manage Partners and Investment Decisions
  

* Partner Management: Select, brief, manage, and evaluate architects, interior designers, engineers, and specialty vendors; set clear expectations for scope, quality, timing, communication, and accountability.
* Value Engineering: Partner with Construction and Real Estate to understand design cost drivers and make value-engineering recommendations.
* Investment Tradeoffs: Balance brand expression, operating performance, durability, cost, schedule, and long-term unit economics in design and specification decisions.
* Performance Tracking: Track design-function performance, capacity, risks, and priorities; use post-project reviews to improve standards, tools, and partner performance.
* Annual Operating Plan: Develop the annual design operating plan in partnership with Real Estate, including internal and consultant capacity, priorities, budget needs, and key risks; provide regular updates on design delivery.

Leadership Competencies
  

* Ownership & Accountability: Sets clear expectations, follows through reliably, and maintains a high bar for quality.
* People Development & Coaching: Builds the capabilities of internal team members and external partners.
* Cross-Functional Partnership: Creates alignment across Operations, Culinary, Facilities, Construction, Real Estate, Marketing, and vendors.
* Creative & Operational Judgment: Balances brand expression with functionality, durability, speed, cost, and unit performance.
* Continuous Improvement: Uses field learning, post-project reviews, and market insight to strengthen standards and systems.
* Clear Decision-Making: Communicates concise recommendations, surfaces risks and tradeoffs, and documents follow-through.
* Strategic Execution: Translates brand strategy into scalable prototypes, standards, plans, and restaurant environments.

Qualifications, Education & Experience
  
  
**Required:**  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Interior Architecture, Interior Design, Environmental Design, Product Design, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in restaurant, retail, hospitality, architecture, interior design, or another related built-environment discipline.
* Leadership: Experience leading a design team, studio, function, or substantial network of external design partners in a fast-moving, multi-project environment.
* Industry Footprint: Significant hands-on experience with restaurant or similarly operationally intensive commercial design, including prototype development, new-unit growth, remodels, and site-specific adaptation.
* Operational Design: Strong command of FOH/BOH flow, kitchen equipment, labor and ergonomics, guest circulation and accessibility, pickup and delivery, food safety, storage, and maintainability.
* Partner Management: Experience managing architects, interior designers, engineers, and specialty vendors against quality, schedule, scope, and budget expectations.
* Technical Knowledge: Working knowledge of construction documentation, design QA/QC, permitting, building and health codes, design detailing, accessibility, shop-drawing review, and constructability.
* Financial Acumen: Fluency with design budgets, cost drivers, value engineering, specification tradeoffs, lifecycle durability, and unit economics.
* Communication: Exceptional written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including concise recommendations and executive-ready presentations.
* Travel: Ability to travel occasionally for market visits, project milestones, and team meetings.

**Preferred:**  

* Proficiency with Bluebeam Revu, Excel, PowerPoint, and project-management platforms.
* Working knowledge of AutoCAD and/or Revit and SketchUp.
* Experience scaling design infrastructure during periods of rapid restaurant growth.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS INCLUDE
  

* Competitive Salary, Bonus, and Equity
* Unlimited Meal Privileges
* Health Care & Wellness Benefits
* HSA/FSA
* Pet Insurance
* Employee Assistance Program
* Commuter Benefits
* 401(k) Plan with Company Match
* Unlimited Paid Vacation
* Note: Benefit offerings may differ based on region, position, and employment type.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
  

* Must be able to lift 25 pounds.
* Ability to sit or stand for 6–8 hours.
* Hand use includes single grasping, fine manipulation, pushing, and pulling.
* Work requires bending, twisting, squatting, and reaching.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & FAIR CHANCE EMPLOYMENT STATEMENT
  
Mendocino Farms is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

title: Director of Learning Design
description:
**About Tergar Schools**

Tergar Schools is a Buddhist-inspired K–12 education nonprofit building a new model of learning (MOL). We operate a pilot school in Kathmandu, Nepal, and are constructing a larger campus in the Yolmo Valley in the Himalayas.

Our model rests on a simple starting point: every child possesses basic goodness and its qualities of awareness, love, compassion, wisdom, and joy. It is our job as educators to help them recognize this and give them tools to sustain it. Our long-term aspiration is to help form people who are resilient, altruistic, and joyful.

We’re now building the next chapter of that work: a comprehensive, fully secular model designed to weave into any school’s existing life — not just our own campuses. Rather than build more schools ourselves, we intend to reach 100+ schools in 4+ countries within five years by helping other schools, secular or religious, adopt the model as their own.

**Why This Role Exists**

Our footprint is growing quickly. Two high-performing private schools will begin piloting our model of learning in 2027. A research lab opens in Nepal with a world-class science team. The interest is real and growing.

What we don’t have yet is a full-time position for building the model itself — the products, courses, training materials, and classroom materials that will constitute MOL — and for leading the team that builds it out.

Today that thinking lives mostly with our Executive Director and the instincts of our founding team. This isn’t sustainable at scale. We need someone who can be fully dedicated to this element of our project: an outside-the-box thinker with real contemplative experience, genuinely excited by the challenge of building an entire family of products from scratch rather than adapting an existing portfolio.

**The Opportunity**

This is a builder’s role. You will not inherit a finished product, a proven training program, or a team. You will build those things — starting hands-on, in the room, with our first two outside partner schools — and then lead the team that takes them to scale.

We have materials. However, none of them is a comprehensive, fully secular contemplative model designed to weave into everything a school already does. That is what you would be building, and there is no template for it.

If you are energized by deciding who you need around you rather than inheriting an org chart, and comfortable being personally in the work now so that later you can hand it to people you have trained this is the position for you. .

**What You’ll Own**

**Building the model**

* Design the teacher training program at the center of the MOL — the core product.
* Build out the materials that make the training usable in a real school. Today we imagine adaptable toolkits fitted by hand to each school, a playbook for staff and administrators, and family-facing materials. That is a starting hypothesis, not a spec — the process of choosing what comes is yours to lead.
* Run the model as a product, not a document. Form real hypotheses about what teachers and schools need, test them in live classrooms, and let what you learn change what gets built.
* Propose what gets built now and what waits — and defend those calls. We hold two commitments at once: build lean, and be the best in the world at this. We call it *Minimum Viable Mastery*. You are the person who makes that real week to week, not just in principle.

**Nailing the first schools**

* Be personally hands-on with our new partner schools in Nepal as they begin onboarding in 2027. You will do this work in tandem with the Executive Director (ED).
* Use what you learn there to define what a stable first phase actually looks like, and build the real template other schools will follow.

**Building your team**

* Decide what team you need, and in what order — a Nepal Country Director and Trainer, Country Coordinators, strategic consultants, instructional designers, a UX researcher, and others as the shape of the work becomes clear (a Head of Training in Nepal is currently being hired).
* The ED and the Director of Operations (DOO) authorize and execute the actual hiring. The judgment about who and when is yours.

**Setting the standard, over time**

* Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and the ED hold final say on model fidelity today. As you build a track record — likely marked by a completed first onboarding cycle with our two partner schools — that authority shifts substantively to you.
* Turn Rinpoche’s two to four multi-day sessions a year into material the team can use again: recorded, distilled, built into training, rather than a remarkable conversation nobody can revisit.

**Working with the evidence**

* Partner with the research lab opening in Nepal in late 2026 — led by Drs. Richard Davidson, Robert Roeser, and Robin Nusslock — translating what they learn into real product and training decisions.

  

**What’s Yours, and What Isn’t**

You own the model and the team you build around you. Three things sit outside that:

* **Fundraising and donor relationships.** A separate role entirely.
* **In-country adaptation and community relationships.** Local teams own this on the ground, but you liaise with them directly and are in very frequent communication.
* **Hiring mechanics.** You decide who you need and when; the DOO handles offers, contracts, and process.

One thing sits in between: **production**. Instructional designers, visual designers, and media support will eventually build finished materials from your direction. You will not be making them yourself for long — but their quality is still on you.

**Who You Are**

**What we’re really looking for**

* **A builder grounded in pedagogy.** Deep pedagogical expertise is essential — you understand how children and adults actually learn, and you've designed for it. What sets you apart is that you build and deliver: you've turned that expertise into programs, curricula, or training that real teachers use. A tech or startup background alongside that is a genuine asset.
* **Fluency in a lean approach to product design.** You can talk concretely about strategic experiments, problem/solution and product/market fit, and validated learning — and you have actually worked that way, not just read about it.
* **Real, lived contemplative experience.** A genuine taste of practice, not necessarily in Tergar’s own lineage, and not merely theoretical familiarity. This is the one non-negotiable that doesn’t bend for the right resume.
* **Comfortable being hands-on first and stepping back later.** Personally in the work with our first schools, then deliberately building the standards and training that let a team carry it without you in the room.
* **Able to build lean and aim to be the best in the world at the same time,** without treating those as a trade-off.

**Experience**

* You bring substantial experience in education — as a teacher, school leader, curriculum developer, or learning designer — and you've built something real from that experience and gotten it into people's hands without much money or staff.
* Some experience directing, mentoring, or building a team from scratch, since you will be doing exactly that here.
* Comfort working directly from a founder’s evolving vision rather than a finished brief — you will be co-writing the brief as you go, especially in the first months.

**Personal qualities**

* Discernment above all: knowing which calls are yours to make outright and which need to go to the Rinpoche or the ED. This carries more weight here than almost any other quality, because for a long stretch there is no layer of management between your judgment and the model’s integrity.
* Genuine curiosity about and respect for a tradition that may not be your own, without needing to adopt it as your own practice.
* Comfortable with ambiguity and a mandate that will keep changing shape under you as the first schools teach you things no one currently knows.

  

**How We Work Together**

* Intensive, hands-on time in Nepal during onboarding and the first deployment of the model. Expect three to five months during the first year.
* Frequent, close contact with the ED for the first six months, settling into a slower rhythm as trust builds.
* Two to four multi-day sessions a year with Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche, alongside the wider team.
* A small, distributed, high-autonomy culture across Vermont, Wisconsin, Ireland, Kathmandu, and Minnesota — deep, steady, skillful work over speed.

  

**Compensation & Logistics**

* Full-time
* Fully remote.
* Compensation: $75,000–$100,000, DOE
* Benefits: flexible schedule, unlimited PTO, and health care reimbursement up to $1,000 per month

title: Director of Marketplaces

This role serves as the primary owner of marketplace, digital shelf, and TikTok Shop execution, working closely with external partners across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Instacart, and priority Asian and mainstream grocery marketplaces.
  
  
As the second member of a two-person team building Calbee America’s digital commerce function, this position requires a hands-on, entrepreneurial approach and comfort operating with ambiguity, particularly during the first six months. The role works closely with the VP, Omnichannel Commerce and has direct visibility to the President.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities:**  
Marketplace & Digital Shelf Performance
  

* Manage day-to-day marketplace operations across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Instacart, and priority Asian retail platforms, including Weee, H Mart, and Yamibuy.
* Maintain account health, catalog accuracy, product listings, product variations, and in-stock availability.
* Optimize digital shelf performance through complete product content, imagery, enhanced content, product attributes, search visibility, ratings, and reviews.
* Establish and maintain a digital shelf health baseline across priority retailers and drive measurable improvement in the composite score.

Retail Media Execution
  

* Execute retail media campaigns against performance targets and return on advertising spend (ROAS) goals established by the VP, Omnichannel Commerce.

description:
**About Trauma Healing Accelerated**

Trauma Healing Accelerated (THA) is an education organization built on the Biology of Trauma® framework developed by Dr. Aimie Apigian, a double board-certified physician and author of *The Biology of Trauma*. The framework explains how unresolved trauma is held in the body and nervous system, and how it can be addressed through a biology-first approach.

THA serves two audiences: individuals pursuing their own healing, and the coaches, therapists and clinicians who support them. Our offerings span free educational resources, including the Biology of Trauma podcast and YouTube channel, through our flagship Foundational Journey, the Biology of Trauma® modules and yearlong programs. All THA offerings are educational in nature and do not constitute medical advice.

* Position: Content & Growth Lead
* Location: Remote (team operates on Pacific Time)
* Reports to: Executive Director of Programs
* Key relationship: Dr. Aimie Apigian, Founder
* Employment type: Contract, full-time hours

**Position overview**

The Content & Growth Lead is accountable for THA's growth engine: the strategy, content and channels through which new audiences discover our work and enroll in our programs. The role holds a comprehensive command of THA's existing content library and determines what should be created, repurposed or reintroduced to market.

This is a strategic leadership position with hands-on responsibility. The Content & Growth Lead sets direction across email marketing, podcast, YouTube, social media, the website, partnerships, speaking and public relations, directs the contributors who execute that work, and owns the weekly performance reporting for each channel. **Email marketing**

title: Director of Marketing
description:
CyberSheath Services International LLC is a rapidly growing Managed Services Provider primarily focused on providing Cybersecurity services to the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). We are excited to be expanding our staff due to our growth and are looking to add a Director of Channel Partnerships & Business Development to our team!

CyberSheath integrates compliance and threat mitigation efforts and eliminates redundant security practices that don't improve and, in fact, may weaken an organization's security posture. Our professionals tell clients where to stop spending, where to invest, and how to take what they are already doing and integrate it in a way that delivers improved security.

Successful candidates for CyberSheath are self-motivated, think out of the box, work, and solve issues independently. Additionally, our most successful people are self-starters and willing to put on many hats in order to succeed. CyberSheath is fast-growing and seeks candidates who want to be part of our upward trajectory.

Position Overview

CyberSheath is seeking a strategic, hands-on Director of Marketing to build and lead a high-performing marketing function during a pivotal period of market growth and increasing CMMC adoption. This leader will own the development and execution of an integrated marketing strategy that strengthens brand authority, creates qualified pipeline, accelerates revenue, and positions CyberSheath as the trusted cybersecurity compliance partner for the Defense Industrial Base.

The Director of Marketing will translate complex cybersecurity, regulatory, and technical concepts into clear, credible, audience-specific messaging that resonates with executive buyers, IT and security leaders, compliance stakeholders, and operational leaders at defense contractors. This person will combine strategic rigor with operational excellence—setting the go-to-market plan while remaining close to campaigns, content, events, demand generation, performance analytics, and sales alignment.

The ideal candidate is a data-driven B2B marketing leader with experience in cybersecurity, managed services, compliance technology, government contracting, or similarly complex technical markets. They are comfortable operating in a growth-stage, private equity-backed environment, understand long sales cycles and multi-stakeholder buying committees, and know how to create measurable marketing impact.

What You'll Do

Marketing Strategy and Go-to-Market

* Develop and lead CyberSheath's annual and quarterly marketing strategy in partnership with executive leadership, sales, solution engineering, customer success, and service delivery.
* Define target segments, ideal customer profiles, buyer personas, market priorities, and account-tiering strategies for defense contractors and subcontractors navigating CMMC, DFARS, and NIST SP 800-171 requirements.
* Build integrated go-to-market plans for CyberSheath's core managed compliance, managed security, managed IT, assessment, implementation, and secure enclave offerings.
* Establish clear marketing priorities, budgets, milestones, operating cadences, and performance expectations tied to company revenue objectives.
* Identify market trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and customer pain points that should inform messaging, campaigns, sales enablement, and product/service positioning.
* Support market expansion and new-service launches with disciplined positioning, audience targeting, launch planning, campaign execution, and performance measurement.

Demand Generation and Revenue Marketing

* Own the demand-generation engine from awareness through opportunity creation, working closely with Sales to drive pipeline quality, velocity, conversion, and revenue contribution.
* Create and optimize multi-channel campaigns across digital advertising, search, email nurture, webinars, content syndication, events, partner marketing, social media, and account-based marketing.
* Design programs that engage key buying-committee members, including CEOs, COOs, CFOs, CISOs, CIOs, IT leaders, compliance leaders, program managers, and operations executives.
* Partner with Sales leadership to define lead stages, service-level agreements, qualification criteria, routing processes, follow-up expectations, and closed-loop reporting.
* Build account-based marketing programs for priority accounts, strategic verticals, and high-value partner ecosystems.
* Develop nurture paths that educate prospective customers on compliance urgency, business risk, assessment readiness, remediation needs, and the operational requirements of maintaining CMMC compliance over time.
* Continuously test audience, channel, message, offer, and conversion-path hypotheses to improve marketing efficiency and pipeline outcomes.

Brand, Messaging, and Content

* Own CyberSheath's brand strategy, voice, positioning, messaging architecture, and narrative across external and internal-facing marketing assets.
* Ensure CyberSheath clearly communicates its differentiation as a specialized, end-to-end cybersecurity compliance partner for defense contractors rather than a generalist technology or security provider.
* Lead development of high-value thought leadership, including executive articles, regulatory explainers, blogs, guides, case studies, solution briefs, webinars, customer stories, analyst-facing content, and event presentations.
* Translate highly technical and regulatory subject matter into accessible, commercially relevant content without sacrificing accuracy or credibility.
* Partner with internal subject-matter experts to develop compelling perspectives on CMMC 2.0, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, secure CUI environments, managed security, assessment readiness, and continuous compliance.
* Maintain a high editorial standard and a consistent content calendar that supports organic demand, customer education, sales enablement, search visibility, and executive thought leadership.
* Oversee website messaging, conversion paths, content governance, SEO priorities, and user experience improvements.

Product and Sales Enablement

* Partner with Sales, Solution Engineering, and Service Delivery to sharpen service positioning, customer value propositions, competitive differentiation, and proof points.
* Develop sales-enablement materials such as pitch decks, battlecards, solution briefs, case studies, industry-specific messaging, objection-handling resources, and customer presentation templates.
* Equip revenue teams with clear, current, and consistent messaging for every stage of the buyer journey.
* Create mechanisms to capture and distribute market intelligence from prospects, customers, partners, competitors, and frontline revenue teams.
* Support customer marketing initiatives, including advocacy, testimonials, referral programs, case studies, and expansion campaigns.

Events, Partnerships, and Field Marketing

* Refine CyberSheath's strategy for industry events, trade shows, conferences, webinars, and executive programs relevant to the DIB, defense contracting, cybersecurity, compliance, and government technology markets.
* Ensure events are planned against measurable objectives, including target-account engagement, meeting generation, pipeline influence, partner activation, and revenue impact.
* Build co-marketing programs with strategic technology, channel, and ecosystem partners, including Microsoft and other organizations serving the compliance and defense-contractor market.
* Identify opportunities for CyberSheath executives and subject-matter experts to build visibility through speaking engagements, contributed content, media opportunities, and industry participation.

Analytics, Operations, and Team Leadership

* Establish a metrics-driven marketing operating model that measures awareness, engagement, marketing-sourced pipeline, marketing-influenced pipeline, conversion rates, customer acquisition cost, campaign ROI, pipeline velocity, and revenue contribution.
* Build and maintain reliable dashboards and executive reporting that clearly communicate marketing performance, key insights, risks, and recommended actions.
* Manage marketing technology, data hygiene, attribution, campaign operations, and budget discipline in partnership with Revenue Operations and other internal stakeholders.
* Evaluate and optimize the marketing technology stack, vendors, agencies, freelancers, and internal resources to ensure efficient execution.
* Hire, develop, coach, and retain a high-performing marketing team as the organization grows.
* Foster a collaborative, accountable, customer-centric culture that values speed, quality, experimentation, commercial impact, and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 6 to 12 months, the Director of Marketing will be expected to:

* Establish a clear, differentiated, and consistent market narrative for CyberSheath and its service portfolio.
* Implement an integrated demand-generation strategy that produces a predictable flow of qualified opportunities.
* Strengthen alignment between Marketing, Sales, Solution Engineering, and Customer Success around target accounts, lead management, messaging, and pipeline goals.
* Improve visibility into marketing performance through practical, trusted funnel and revenue reporting.
* Elevate CyberSheath's thought-leadership presence in the CMMC, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, and broader DIB cybersecurity compliance market.
* Build a scalable content engine that supports organic growth, outbound sales efforts, customer education, and partner engagement.
* Improve conversion across core marketing journeys, including website engagement, webinar registration, gated-content conversion, demo requests, assessment inquiries, and sales-accepted leads.
* Establish a repeatable field, event, and partner-marketing framework tied to measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in marketing, business, communications, or a related field; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* 8+ years of progressive B2B marketing experience, including 3+ years in a marketing leadership role.
* Demonstrated success developing and executing marketing strategies that drive measurable pipeline, revenue, and market growth.
* Experience marketing complex B2B services, technology solutions, cybersecurity offerings, managed services, compliance solutions, SaaS, or enterprise IT services.
* Strong command of demand generation, account-based marketing, content strategy, digital marketing, field marketing, campaign operations, and marketing analytics.
* Experience supporting sales organizations with long, complex sales cycles and multiple economic, technical, and operational stakeholders.
* Proven ability to translate technical concepts into customer-focused positioning, messaging, and content.
* Strong executive communication, presentation, writing, and stakeholder-management skills.
* Experience managing budgets, agencies, vendors, and marketing technology platforms.
* Track record of building and leading high-performing teams in fast-moving, growth-oriented environments.
* Analytical mindset and fluency with funnel metrics, attribution, conversion analysis, pipeline reporting, and campaign performance optimization.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in cybersecurity, cybersecurity compliance, managed security services, managed IT services, GRC, risk management, or regulated technology markets.
* Familiarity with the Defense Industrial Base, federal contracting, CMMC 2.0, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, FedRAMP, CUI, or government cloud environments.
* Experience marketing to defense contractors, manufacturers, engineering firms, federal contractors, or regulated mid-market organizations.
* Experience working in a private equity-backed or high-growth business environment.
* Familiarity with CRM, marketing automation, web analytics, SEO, paid media, intent-data, ABM, and attribution tools.
* Experience launching services, entering new markets, repositioning a brand, or scaling a marketing organization.

Work Environment

* Fully remote role with occasional travel for industry events and offsite meetings

*CyberSheath is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with a disability.*

title: Director of Brand
description:
**About this role**
-------------------

Boulder Care is hiring its first Director of Brand to own how trust is built with the people and communities we serve. You will lead the brand, content and creative system that makes Boulder's promise clear and credible, from our digital positioning and patient stories to campaigns, social, community partnerships and the materials that help people choose care.

This is a builder role. You will have the opportunity to create and mature a brand machine. You will turn a new messaging platform and visual refresh into a working system, lead a team and trusted external partners, and build a clear brand investment strategy with learning loops. You will report to the Chief Growth Officer and partner closely with Communications, Product, Clinical, and Commercial leadership.

**About Boulder**
-----------------

Boulder Care is an award-winning digital clinic for addiction medicine, recognized for both innovation and high-quality patient care. Founded in 2017 by CEO Stephanie Strong, our mission is to improve the lives of people with substance use disorders through compassionate, evidence-based care.

We provide Boulder patients with a fully virtual, multidisciplinary care team, including medical providers and peer recovery specialists, who deliver personalized treatment, such as medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) and ongoing support. Our approach is grounded in clinical excellence, patient-centered care, and a commitment to reducing barriers to recovery. Boulder partners with leading health plans, employers, and community organizations to ensure that our services are accessible and covered for the people who need them most.

Named by Fortune as one of the Best Workplaces in Healthcare, we foster a culture of kindness, respect, and meaningful work that delivers outstanding patient outcomes and moves the addiction medicine industry forward.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Own Boulder's brand positioning, visual identity, voice and editorial point of view across the full journey.
* Lead the brand, creative and content team: set priorities, give clear direction, develop people and manage external designers, production partners and agencies.
* Build the trust-content engine to power a unique market position: patients, peers and clinicians; reviews/social proof; owned content; creator programs; and a compliant content-to-distribution plan.
* Run Boulder's brand portfolio with a thesis, activation plan, budget discipline, measurement approach and renewal gate for every material investment.
* Translate a visual identity and messaging guide into an easy-to-use creative system: templates, channel guidance, campaign frameworks, art direction, and self-service guardrails.
* Own creative strategy and production: brand launches, community partnerships, sponsorships, executive platforms, web and priority activations.
* Use AI responsibly to increase speed and consistency while protecting clinical accuracy, human judgment and Boulder's voice.

**What you bring**
------------------

* 10+ years in consumer brand, creative, content or integrated marketing leadership, including leadership of an internal team and external partners.
* Exceptional creative taste and judgment across identity, campaign, editorial, social-native video, web and high-stakes storytelling.
* Experience directing creative production and getting high-quality work from a constrained budget and small team.
* Strong operating muscle: clear briefs, prioritization, budget ownership, vendor management and outcome-based reporting.
* Experience with creator, community or customer-story programs and a strong instinct for editorial trust and consent.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Proven AI fluency and sound judgment about where automation helps.

**Nice to have**
----------------

* Experience turning a human or emotionally complex category into trusted, differentiated creative work; healthcare, behavioral health, advocacy or another regulated category is a plus.
* Experience with Figma, Adobe CC, Canva, Frame.io, Air or a similar suite of tools is a plus.

**Work environment**
--------------------

* This is a full-time, 100% remote position. Availability during standard business hours is expected, with flexibility to support business needs.
* Travel up to 15% is expected for team gatherings, production, partnership activations and key company events.
* Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.
* Office requirements: Boulder teammates working with sensitive information must have a dedicated, private workspace with a lockable door and high-speed internet to maintain a secure, distraction-free environment, ensuring compliance with HIPAA and confidentiality standards.
* Boulder Care employees are free to use our riverfront HQ located in Portland, OR, whenever they would like.

**Compensation**
----------------

The starting pay range for this position is **$175,000–$190,000**; base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave).

**Perks and benefits**
----------------------

* Contribute to meaningful, life-saving work!
* Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and short-term disability benefits designed to take care of our employees and their families
* Mental health services via insurance coverage, including Talkspace and EAP for continuous care
* 4 weeks of vacation accrued per calendar year with a tenured increase to 5 weeks at 2 years of employment
* Sick leave accrued at 1 hr for every 30 hrs paid
* 9 paid holidays per year
* 12 weeks of 100% paid parental leave for the birth or adoption of a child (after 6 months of employment)
* 401(k) retirement savings
* Remote work with company-provided hardware

**Our values**
--------------

* Patients always come first
* Our opportunity is also our duty
* Move the industry forward, follow the data
* Facts to change minds, empathy to change hearts
* Turn bold ideas into even bolder action
* Strong individuals, stronger together
* Boulder Care recognizes the value that **lived experience** can provide to our organization, community, and patients. Applicants with lived experience and/or training as a peer recovery specialist are encouraged to apply.

*Boulder Care believes the people who manage our product and team should be representative of those who use the platform. This includes people from backgrounds that are historically underrepresented in the industry. We celebrate differences and are committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or veteran status. If you are a qualified person with a passion for what we do, please apply!*

title: Director, Enterprise Communications
description:
**Who We Are**

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

**What We Build**

Our products—**Eureka Math and** Eureka Math², **Wit & Wisdom**, **Geodes**, and the newly launched **Arts & Letters ELA**—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

* **Eureka Math** is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.
* **Wit & Wisdom®** and **Arts & Letters ELA™** anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. **Geodes®** complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

**Where We’re Headed**

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.

**Job Purpose**

Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Communications, the Director, Enterprise Communicationswill act as a senior leader responsible for the strategy, execution, and continuous evolution of Great Minds’ internal communications and employer brand functions. Internally, this role will shape how the organization communicates at an enterprise level, ensuring employees are informed, connected to strategy and values, and inspired by the mission and impact that drive Great Minds’ work. Externally, this role will curate, monitor, and disseminate content that tells the story of Great Minds’ mission, culture and values to support recruiting, retention, and sales. The Director will serve as the company’s chief architect of enterprise communication, setting the vision for how the company reaches, engages, and retains a dispersed, impact-driven workforce; positioning Great Minds as an employer of choice; and ensuring internal stories reach external audiences where they can reinforce our brand and reputation.

**Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership and Team Management:
  + Lead and develop the Internal Communications function, providing strategic direction, coaching, and clear accountability for goals and quality standards.
  + Set the enterprise communications vision and annual strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, culture, and the 2030 student outcomes commitment.
  + Serve as a senior strategic advisor to executive leadership and the VP, Corporate Communications, translating organizational priorities into communications approaches that build clarity, trust, and engagement.
  + Partner deeply across functions to drive alignment, inform communications, and source stories—including HR and Strategy to convey operating values and organizational direction; Research, Product, Sales, and Customer Success to surface impact data and field stories that connect employees to the difference Great Minds makes for students and educators; and Brand, Marketing, and Legal to ensure consistency, accuracy, and voice across all enterprise communications.
* Enterprise Communications:
  + Own the enterprise-wide internal communications framework—including editorial calendar, governance, channel strategy, and content standards—that keeps employees informed and connected to what matters most.
  + Lead communications for high-stakes, organization-wide moments: executive announcements, leadership transitions, strategic initiatives, transformation efforts, and town halls.
  + Ensure employees have consistent access to need-to-know operational information while also deepening their connection to Great Minds’ strategy, culture, values, and impact.
  + Build and steward a center of excellence model, equipping communications liaisons and cross-functional partners with tools, frameworks, and best practices to strengthen the quality of communications across the organization.
  + Build and operate an employee storytelling engine—partnering with teams that include Product, Research, Sales, and Customer Success to identify, develop, and distribute compelling stories of student and educator impact that connect Great Minds employees to the purpose behind their work.
  + Work closely with HR and Strategy to develop communications that actively convey Great Minds’ operating values, culture commitments, and strategic direction—ensuring employees understand not just what the organization is doing, but why it matters and how they contribute.
  + Develop and implement measurement frameworks (KPIs, engagement data, feedback loops) to continuously assess and improve internal communications effectiveness.
  + Lead the embedding of Great Minds’ refreshed enterprise brand across internal channels and communications—partnering with Brand to ensure voice, visual identity, and messaging standards are consistently reflected in all employee-facing content and experiences.
* Platform and Channel Evolution:
  + Partner with IT on Great Minds’ internal communications technology roadmap—evaluating, selecting, and optimizing platforms, tools, and formats to enhance reach, usability, and employee experience.
  + Bring technical fluency to channel strategy decisions, including intranet architecture, email platforms, video tools, and emerging collaboration and communications technologies.
  + Drive adoption and governance of communication platforms, ensuring tools are used effectively and equitably across a distributed workforce.
  + Identify gaps in current channel infrastructure and develop phased recommendations for platform evolution that serve both near-term needs and long-term scalability.
* Employer Brand and Internal Storytelling:
  + Build and lead Great Minds’ employer brand strategy, positioning the organization as a destination for mission-aligned talent and amplifying the employee experience externally.
  + Identify compelling internal stories—from educator impact to employee milestones to culture moments—and develop them into external-facing content in partnership with Media Relations and Brand.
  + Create and sustain an employee storytelling engine that amplifies authentic stories from across the organization to showcase mission impact internally and externally.
  + Collaborate with Media Relations to pitch employee and culture stories to relevant media and talent-focused outlets, expanding the reach of Great Minds’ employer brand.
  + Own Great Minds’ employer reputation strategy—including active management of Glassdoor, LinkedIn employer presence, and other third-party platforms—monitoring sentiment, responding to reviews, and developing proactive strategies to strengthen how the organization is perceived as a place to work.
  + Ensure employer brand messaging is consistent and compelling across internal and external channels, including LinkedIn, Glassdoor, and recruiting materials.
  + Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to develop communications that support the full employee lifecycle—attraction, onboarding, engagement, and retention.

**Requirements**

* 7+ years of progressive experience in communications or marketing, with demonstrated ownership of enterprise-wide strategy
* 5+ years of management experience
* Experience managing or mentoring direct reports, with a track record of developing talent and building high-functioning teams
* Experience developing or contributing to employer brand strategy, with an understanding of how internal culture stories translate to external reputation
* Demonstrated experience managing employer reputation on platforms such as Glassdoor and LinkedIn, including proactive review strategy, sentiment monitoring, and response frameworks
* Experience building employee or customer storytelling programs that surface and amplify narratives of impact across internal and external channels
* Experience partnering with brand or creative teams to embed refreshed brand identities into internal communications—including voice, visual standards, and messaging frameworks
* Proven ability to advise and influence senior executives, translating complex organizational priorities into compelling, accessible messaging
* Deep expertise in executive communications, change and transformation communications, and large-scale organizational initiatives
* Strong technical knowledge of internal communications platforms and channel ecosystems—including intranets, email platforms, video tools, and collaboration technology—with the ability to evaluate and recommend platform investments
* Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone across formats, audiences, and channels
* Strong project management skills and the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in a communications function at an education or mission-driven entity
* Familiarity with media relations related to employer brand and culture storytelling
* Experience building or transforming an internal communications function, including platform migrations or channel strategy overhauls
* Track record of using data and analytics to measure communications effectiveness and drive continuous improvement

**Required Education**

Bachelor’s degree

**Preferred Education**

Bachelor’s degree with a focus in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing, Journalism, Business, or a related field

**Status**

Full-time

**Location**

Remote

The expected base salary range for this position is $164,000-$180,000, however the offered salarymay be higher or lower than the above range dependent on numerous factors including, but not limited to location, work experience, skills and internal equity considerations. The base salary is not inclusive of benefits or other incentives.

A cover letter and resume are required to be considered for this position.

New employees will be required to successfully complete a background check.

Any communication to applicants relating to the Great Minds hiring process will only come from email addresses with the domains **greatminds.org** or **greatminds.recruitee.com**. If in the course of the application or hiring process with Great Minds you are contacted through another domain, are requested to provide banking or other sensitive information, or you note any other suspicious activity, please contact security@greatminds.org

Great Minds is an equal opportunity employer. We will extend equal opportunity to all individuals without regard to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, disability, age, genetic information, or any other status protected under applicable federal, state, or local laws. Our policy reflects and affirms the organization’s commitment to the principles of fair employment and the elimination of all discriminatory practices.

title: Senior CRM Marketing Operations Analyst
description:
**Description**

**Salary Range: $90,000 - $110,000**

**About Designs for Health**  
Designs for Health is a trusted leader in the nutraceutical industry, known for delivering high-quality, research-driven nutritional products that support better health outcomes. For more than 30 years, we have combined scientific integrity, innovation, and a strong commitment to quality to earn the confidence of practitioners and customers alike.

**Job Summary**

We are seeking a detail-oriented, analytical Senior CRM Marketing Operations Analyst to serve as the functional owner and power user for Marketing's use of HubSpot. This remote role combines CRM operations, marketing analytics, and email and SMS execution to support business-to-business (B2B), patient-focused business-to-consumer (B2C), and direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels.

The analyst owns Marketing-facing HubSpot processes, workflows, audiences, dashboards, campaign operations, and user enablement while partnering with Brand Leads, copywriters, Creative, Sales, IT, and other business teams. The role collaborates with the Senior CRM Sales Operations Analyst on shared customer and account data, lifecycle definitions, lead handoffs, integrations, and cross-functional reporting. The role also connects sales outcomes with customer insights while providing analysis, segmentation, and measurement support to campaign and lifecycle strategy owners.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Serve as the functional owner, senior power user, and subject matter expert for Marketing's use of HubSpot, including marketing processes, properties, lists, workflows, reports, dashboards, documentation, and usage standards.
* Analyze CRM, campaign, customer, and marketing-engagement data across B2B, patient-focused B2C, and DTC channels to identify trends, opportunities, and actionable insights.
* Build and maintain Marketing-facing HubSpot reports, dashboards, and performance summaries for Brand, Marketing, Customer Service, and leadership stakeholders; collaborate with the Sales CRM counterpart on shared funnel and revenue reporting.
* Coordinate with Brand Leads to define and maintain the strategic email and SMS content calendar, campaign schedule, automated flows, and related operational requirements.
* Coordinate with Brand Leads, copywriters, and Creative partners to move email and SMS content through development and ensure required copy, creative assets, audience criteria, and campaign details are ready for execution.
* Build, schedule, quality-check, and execute email and SMS campaigns and automated flows in HubSpot and connected tools, ensuring accurate audiences, links, timing, and tracking.
* Measure email and SMS performance, audience engagement, lead quality, conversion activity, and customer lifecycle outcomes and translate results into actionable recommendations.
* Develop and refine customer segments, targeting logic, campaign lists, suppression criteria, and audience-performance analysis in partnership with Brand Leads and other marketing stakeholders.
* Maintain and improve the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of Marketing-owned CRM data, including audience, consent, campaign, engagement, and marketing-touchpoint information; coordinate changes to shared contact and company data with the Sales CRM counterpart.
* Own Marketing's business requirements and operational support for HubSpot integrations with marketing automation, business intelligence, and other connected systems; coordinate shared integrations and data flows with the Sales CRM counterpart, IT, Data, and system owners.
* Monitor and troubleshoot Marketing-facing CRM data discrepancies, workflow issues, integration errors, and reporting inconsistencies; partner with the Sales CRM counterpart and technical owners when issues affect shared data or processes.
* Establish and improve governance for Marketing-owned HubSpot processes, including audience and consent standards, naming conventions, campaign tracking, workflow documentation, and marketing data quality; jointly maintain shared lifecycle and handoff definitions with Sales.
* Provide HubSpot guidance, training, and documentation for Marketing users that promote adoption, consistent campaign practices, data discipline, and reliable decision-making.
* Collaborate with the broader Marketing team to support departmental initiatives, projects, and evolving business priorities as needed.

**Competency**

* **HubSpot Expertise:** Applies advanced platform knowledge to reporting, segmentation, workflows, email and SMS execution, data quality, integrations, and user enablement.
* **Analytical Thinking:** Interprets campaign, customer, CRM, and sales data and translates findings into practical recommendations.
* **Marketing Operations Acumen:** Understands email and SMS calendars, content workflows, campaign execution, audience segmentation, customer journeys, and performance measurement.
* **Cross-Functional Coordination:** Keeps Brand Leads, copywriters, Creative partners, and technical stakeholders aligned on requirements, timing, dependencies, and execution readiness.
* **Data Accuracy & Governance:** Maintains strong attention to detail and promotes clean, structured, well-governed customer data.
* **Systems Thinking:** Understands how customer data flows across HubSpot and connected marketing, sales, ERP, and reporting platforms.
* **Communication & Collaboration:** Works effectively across Marketing, Sales, IT, Data, and other business teams and establishes clear ownership for shared CRM processes.
* **Problem Solving:** Investigates root causes and recommends practical improvements to marketing data, campaign workflows, integrations, and reporting.
* **Process Orientation:** Creates repeatable practices, clear documentation, and consistent standards for CRM analytics and operations.
* **Adaptability:** Adjusts effectively to changing business priorities, evolving systems, and fast-moving marketing needs.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Data Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* 5+ years of hands-on experience in CRM operations, marketing operations, lifecycle marketing, marketing analytics, customer data, or campaign execution and reporting.
* Required advanced, hands-on HubSpot experience, including reports and dashboards, segmentation, workflows, properties, lifecycle stages, data quality, email and SMS execution, and connected applications.
* Experience coordinating email and SMS content calendars, automated flows, audience segmentation, campaign quality assurance, scheduling, execution, and performance reporting.
* Experience coordinating content development with Brand Leads, copywriters, Creative teams, and other stakeholders while managing campaign requirements and timelines.
* Experience supporting CRM integrations, monitoring data flows, and troubleshooting synchronization or data-quality issues across connected systems.
* Strong working knowledge of Excel and/or Google Sheets; experience with Power BI, Looker, Tableau, or a similar business intelligence tool is a plus.
* Working knowledge of CRM data structures, lead and customer lifecycle stages, marketing funnels, email and SMS campaign tracking, and customer segmentation.
* Ability to analyze, synthesize, and present complex CRM, campaign, and customer data in clear business language and translate stakeholder questions into reporting, segmentation, workflow, and data solutions.
* Experience partnering with Sales Operations on lifecycle definitions, lead handoffs, shared data governance, integrations, and cross-functional reporting is preferred.
* Understanding of data privacy, CRM governance, and email and SMS marketing compliance considerations, including CAN-SPAM and related best practices.
* Experience in nutraceuticals, CPG, healthcare, wellness, or another regulated or quality-focused environment is preferred.

**Benefits**

* You receive a competitive salary and performance-based incentives.
* You benefit from health, dental, and vision insurance plans.
* You receive a monthly product stipend to support your personal health journey.
* You have access to paid time off and company holidays.
* You work in a collaborative and supportive team environment.

**Physical Demands**

This position is primarily sedentary, requiring regular computer use and communication. Some tasks may involve moving within the office environment or occasional lifting of up to 10 lbs. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential duties.

**Privacy**

Your application for this position is subject to Designs for Health's Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Workforce Members. Designs for Health does not sell your personal information, nor does Designs for Health share it for purposes of cross-context behavioral advertising.

**Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging**

Designs for Health is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all employees can grow and thrive. Our employees form meaningful and often life-long connections while working at Designs for Health. We are all passionate about our mission of designing a well world together.

title: Director, Editorial and Engagement
description:
**Who We Are**
==============

Clean Air Task Force (CATF) is a global nonprofit organization working to safeguard against the worst impacts of climate change by catalyzing the rapid development and deployment of low-carbon energy and other climate-protecting technologies. With 30 years of internationally recognized expertise on climate policy and a fierce commitment to exploring all potential solutions, CATF is a pragmatic, non-ideological advocacy group with the bold ideas needed to address climate change. CATF has offices in Boston, Washington, D.C., and Brussels, with staff working virtually around the world.

**What You'll Do**
==================

CATF works to accelerate the solutions needed to achieve a zero-emissions future. As a senior leader within the Communications & Marketing team, you will shape how CATF tells its story, elevates its ideas and experts, and engages the audiences that can help turn climate and energy solutions into real-world impact.

You will bring together institutional storytelling, executive communications, strategic events, media relations, and other important communications opportunities. Working across CATF, you will help determine which stories we tell, where and how we show up, and how our communications support organizational priorities.

This role will build an integrated editorial and engagement strategy that connects CATF's expertise with policymakers, industry leaders, donors, media, and other influential audiences.

### **Responsibilities**

* **Editorial Strategy & Institutional Storytelling** – Develop and carry out CATF's organization-wide editorial strategy and content calendar, turning organizational priorities and technical expertise into clear, compelling stories for priority audiences.
* **Messaging, Voice & Editorial Standards** – Maintain CATF's organizational messaging, editorial standards, voice, and style guidance so communications are accurate, accessible, consistent, and aligned with CATF's brand.
* **Flagship Content Leadership** – Lead or guide major institutional content, including CATF's annual report, organizational and program milestones, impact case studies, and other high-profile content.
* **Strategic Events & External Engagement** – Develop an organization-wide approach to priority events and engagements, including conferences, climate weeks, convenings, speaking opportunities, roundtables, executive engagements, and CATF-led events. Help determine the audience, messaging, speakers, content, and communications strategy for each opportunity.
* **Executive Communications & Thought Leadership** – Develop communications strategies for CATF executives and senior experts. Identify opportunities and produce speeches, opinion pieces, commentary, presentations, talking points, and other executive communications.
* **Media Relations & Reputation Building** – Work with Communications & Marketing colleagues to build relationships with influential journalists and outlets, elevate CATF's experts, and provide communications counsel during major media moments and sensitive or reputational issues.
* **Integrated Content & Engagement Planning** – Connect CATF's editorial, media, executive communications, and event strategies through an integrated planning process tied to organizational priorities and audience needs.
* **People Leadership & Team Development** – Supervise, coach, and develop communications staff. Set clear priorities and standards while supporting independent judgment, collaboration, and professional growth.

**What You'll Bring**
=====================

You are an experienced communications leader, writer, editor, convener, and strategist who understands how strong ideas become useful stories, conversations, and engagements. You can make complex climate, energy, technical, and policy issues clear without losing important context.

You bring sound editorial judgment and a collaborative leadership style. You can advise senior leaders, develop staff, and build alignment across functions, cultures, geographies, and time zones.

### **Required Experience**

* Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
* 10–15 years of progressively responsible experience in strategic communications, editorial leadership, media relations, journalism, public affairs, external engagement, or a related field.
* Strong English-language writing, editing, and storytelling skills, including experience translating complex technical or policy issues into clear communications.
* Demonstrated expertise in editorial strategy, institutional storytelling, organizational messaging, and high-profile content.
* Significant experience developing executive communications and thought leadership, including speeches, opinion pieces, commentary, presentations, talking points, or other executive-level content.
* Experience developing proactive media relations strategies, working directly with journalists and editors, and advising on sensitive, rapid-response, or reputational communications.
* Experience developing strategic events and external engagements, including conferences, convenings, executive engagements, speaking opportunities, or similar forums.
* People leadership and cross-functional collaboration experience, including supervising and developing staff, advising senior leaders, and working with technical experts, policy professionals, development teams, and communications colleagues.

### **Preferred Experience**

* Experience with climate and energy policy, advocacy, policymaking, environmental policy, clean technology, science, or a closely related field.
* Familiarity with engagement strategies for major international climate, energy, policy, business, or philanthropic forums.
* Experience developing editorial or event content for donors, funders, and other philanthropic audiences.
* Experience working in a global or geographically distributed organization.
* Experience in a nonprofit, think tank, research institution, philanthropic organization, government, journalism, or a similarly mission-driven environment.
* Additional language skills.

**What We Provide**
===================

Join a team working to accelerate climate solutions while improving how CATF shares its work and engages the audiences that can help move it forward.

* A mission-driven role shaping how CATF communicates its work and engages influential audiences.
* Opportunities to collaborate with recognized experts and senior leaders on climate, technology, energy, and policy issues.
* Cross-functional work with Communications & Marketing, Development, executive leadership, and CATF's programs and regions.
* A collaborative and intellectually curious culture where diverse perspectives are valued and bold, practical solutions to climate change are encouraged.
* A flexible remote working environment, with a preference for candidates based in the United States and the ability to work effectively across U.S. and European time zones.
* Periodic domestic and international travel for CATF meetings, conferences, strategic events, media opportunities, and other organizational priorities.
* Benefits designed to support health, financial security, time away, and flexibility.

**Compensation & Pay Transparency**

CATF believes candidates should have clear information about compensation and benefits so they can make informed decisions about opportunities with us. Our compensation ranges are based on the country of employment, and employees are paid in the applicable local currency. Any range listed below applies only to the country identified. For candidates working in other approved countries, compensation will be determined using the applicable local range, taking into account relevant market factors, role scope and responsibilities, experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity.

  

The expected base salary range for this position is:

* **United States: $147,137–$176,565 USD annually**

CATF does not consider an applicant's salary history when determining compensation.

**Benefits**

For U.S.-based employees, CATF offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support health, financial security, time away, and flexibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, with CATF currently paying 80% of medical premiums and 100% of dental premiums for eligible employees; a 401(k) plan with a dollar-for-dollar employer match of up to 5% of gross annual salary; 25 working days of vacation per year for full-time employees; paid sick leave; U.S. holidays; and one flex day in December. CATF also provides employer-paid basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage, along with home-office setup support, a monthly internet stipend, and additional health, wellness, and voluntary benefit resources. Eligibility, coverage, costs, and plan terms are governed by applicable plan documents.

  

**Ready to Apply?**
===================

If you've made it this far, you should go ahead and apply.

You don't need to meet every requirement to be a strong candidate. If this role aligns with how you like to work and the kind of impact you want to have, we encourage you to submit your application.

**Equal Opportunity Statement**
===============================

Clean Air Task Force is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Payer Account Manager
description:
**Payer Account Manager**  
**Location: Remote**

Thea Pharma Inc. is the newly established US commercial organization of French-based pharmaceutical company, Laboratoires Théa (Clermont-Ferrand). Thea Pharma markets a suite of leading eye-care drugs that have been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), including CYKLX™, ZOLYMBUS™, IYUZEH™, Zioptan®, Cosopt®, Cosopt® PF, Azasite®, Akten®, and Betimol®, as well as AcellFX™ Acellular Amniotic Membrane and the portfolio of iVIZIA dry-eye drops and eyelid hygiene products. By focusing its parent company’s passion and expertise within the U.S. market, Thea Pharma’s goal is to deliver uncompromising care that enables all stakeholders to envision the future of ophthalmic treatment with eyes wide open.
